accepted_edits.reason: the v207 edit answers the review's one finding: §51's live check can now fail at the base revision

findings.reason: as written a worker lands §51 with a live check that was already green before the change, so the one measure of the defect's own symptom proves nothing; the section needs a live check on a declared backend command that is not already on the hold PATH, or an assertion that a non-interactive step's composed PATH carries the declared directory.
findings.text: §51's "live check after landing, from a non-interactive step in the fleet job, reads `command -v codex` resolving" cannot fail: running it at the base revision with the migration's own recorded PATH (`~/bin:~/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/sbin`) returns `/home/ITER/mcintos/.local/bin/codex` with exit 0, because the section states a session linked codex into `~/.local/bin` by hand at 07:38Z on 14 November, and only a run without `~/.local/bin` on PATH returns exit 1 — so the check reports the manual mitigation, not the fix, and passes for a migration that composes no environment at all

response_events.note: §51's live check now composes a hold from a /usr/bin:/bin submitter, removes ~/.local/bin from the PATH its services start with, and records the base revision failing beside the fix

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §49's `--no-watch` flag exists (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1432`), its `command_found` claim matches `reckon/flight.py:2458` (a command on a declared search path reports found), §50's cited run has a surviving promotion-request record (`~/.config/reckon/crew/promotion-requests/r-20261113T140142834510-review-of-needs-you-replaces-halted-059feccf91a4.json`) though its run directory was cleaned up, and §51's `~/.npm/packages/bin/codex`, `~/.local/bin/codex` and `/work/projects/imas_gpu/agents` all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §51's post-landing live check (`command -v codex`) already succeeds at the base revision because the manual `~/.local/bin` link the section itself describes puts codex on the migration's PATH.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each of the three gates runs on `all_debug` and its log is recorded in the plan's evidence fragment (`docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html`, which exists), not in a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new units name no code symbol, plan label or ticket number, and their prose describes mechanisms (a PATH composed by a non-interactive submit, a pointer kept for a changed run) rather than a tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §51's stated root cause matches the cited evidence (`~/.bashrc:59` returns for non-interactive shells above the PATH block at lines 66–77, and the recorded job PATH omits `~/.npm/packages/bin`), §49's claim that the flight view resolves a declared-search-path command is what `reckon/flight.py:2458–2503` does, each endpoint is obtainable and its measure can fail, and none of the three prescribes a code path, step sequence or function for the worker to implement.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the three nodes delivers one endpoint (a dispatch route that uses the resolved command; a review run never held for a landing repair; a fleet move that never leaves a declared backend unfindable), and §51's two limbs are prevention and cure of that one endpoint rather than two independent deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §49, §50 and §51 are each declared implementable and each is named by an open followup (f-wftl-017 names §49 and §51's sibling §50, f-wftl-018 names §51 and §49); §49/§50/§51 declare no section waits and need none, and §51's `data-links` target `work-flows-to-the-lane#s49` resolves to a section that exists.
